mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares the coefficients of static (μ_s) and kinetic (μ_k) friction for the same pair of surfaces?
mcqs.explanation: For any pair of surfaces, the maximum static friction that can act before motion starts (μ_s N) is generally larger than the kinetic friction that acts once sliding begins (μ_k N). Hence μ_s > μ_k. Option A is false because the coefficients are not equal; Option C reverses the correct inequality; Option D is incorrect because rough surfaces have non‑zero coefficients.

mcqs.question: A block of mass 5 kg rests on a rough inclined plane. The coefficient of static friction is 0.60 and that of kinetic friction is 0.40. What is the minimum angle (in degrees) of the incline at which the block will just start to slide down?
mcqs.explanation: The block begins to slide when the component of weight down the plane equals the maximum static friction: mg sinθ = μ_s mg cosθ ⇒ tanθ = μ_s. Hence θ = arctan(0.60) ≈ 31°. Option A (30°) is slightly low, C and D are far higher than required.

mcqs.question: The frictional force acting between two surfaces in contact is:

options.B: Always opposite to the direction of relative motion or the tendency of relative motion
options.D: Always greater than the normal force

mcqs.answer: Always opposite to the direction of relative motion or the tendency of relative motion
mcqs.explanation: Friction always acts to oppose relative motion (or the tendency for it) between the contacting surfaces. It equals μ N only when the surfaces are sliding (kinetic friction) or when static friction has reached its limiting value. Options A, C, and D are incorrect statements.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes static friction from kinetic friction?

options.A: Static friction acts when the surfaces are already moving relative to each other
options.B: Kinetic friction is generally larger than static friction for the same pair of surfaces
options.C: Static friction adjusts up to a maximum value to prevent motion, whereas kinetic friction has a constant value once motion starts
options.D: Kinetic friction does not depend on the normal reaction

mcqs.answer: Static friction adjusts up to a maximum value to prevent motion, whereas kinetic friction has a constant value once motion starts
mcqs.explanation: Static friction can vary from zero up to its limiting value μ_s N to oppose an applied force, preventing motion. Once sliding begins, kinetic friction is approximately constant at μ_k N. Options A and B reverse the definitions, and D is false because kinetic friction also depends on the normal force.

mcqs.question: Limiting friction is:

options.A: The maximum value of static friction just before motion starts
options.B: The minimum value of kinetic friction during sliding
options.C: The frictional force when the contacting surfaces are perfectly smooth
options.D: The frictional force equal to the weight of the object

mcqs.answer: The maximum value of static friction just before motion starts
mcqs.explanation: Limiting (or maximum static) friction is the greatest static frictional force that can act before the surfaces begin to slide. It is given by μ_s N. Options B, C, and D describe unrelated concepts.

mcqs.question: A 2 kg block rests on a horizontal rough surface. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the surface is 0.30. What is the magnitude of the kinetic frictional force acting on the block? (Take g = 9.8 m s⁻²)
mcqs.explanation: F_f = μ_k N = μ_k mg = 0.30 × 2 kg × 9.8 m s⁻² = 5.88 N ≈ 5.9 N. The other options result from incorrect multiplication or omission of the mass or g.

mcqs.question: Two surfaces have a coefficient of static friction μ_s = 0.50 and a coefficient of kinetic friction μ_k = 0.35. Which of the following statements is correct?
mcqs.explanation: For any pair of surfaces, the static coefficient is typically larger than the kinetic coefficient, as reflected by the given values (0.50 > 0.35). Options A and B contradict the data, and D is obviously false.

mcqs.question: A 4 kg block is placed on a rough inclined plane that makes an angle of 20° with the horizontal. The coefficients of static and kinetic friction are μ_s = 0.40 and μ_k = 0.30 respectively. The block will:
mcqs.explanation: The component of weight down the plane is mg sin20° = 4 × 9.8 × sin20° ≈ 13.4 N. The maximum static friction available is μ_s N = μ_s mg cos20° ≈ 0.40 × 4 × 9.8 × cos20° ≈ 15.0 N. Since the required friction (13.4 N) is less than the maximum static friction (15.0 N), the block does not move. Hence it remains at rest. Options B, C, and D are inconsistent with the force analysis.
